_comment: Canonical CSV-cell serialisation contract shared by the backend (hexa.core.csv.stringify_cell) and the frontend (DataStudioEditor/csv.ts buildCsv). Each vector is a single value and the exact CSV field it must serialise to (post-guard, post-quote). Both export paths are asserted against this same file so they cannot drift. Only JSON-representable values live here: type-specific branches that never cross the GraphQL wire (Python bytes/Decimal/datetime) are covered by backend-only tests. Numbers beyond the JS safe range are represented as strings, mirroring how NUMERIC/DECIMAL/bigint actually reach the frontend.

vectors.description: ordinary text that merely looks number-ish is not guarded
negative integer number is not an injection risk
big numeric string preserved beyond JS safe int
leading - on non-numeric text is guarded
number-looking but non-numeric leading - is guarded
value with a comma is quoted
embedded double quotes are doubled and quoted
guarded and quoted together (leading - plus comma)
object serialises to compact JSON, then quoted
array serialises to compact JSON, then quoted
